subject: Copywriting
title: Joanna Wiebe: Conversion Copywriting
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Joanna Wiebe: Conversion Copywriting.

hook.text: Joanna Wiebe coined 'conversion copywriting'—a method where every word on a page exists to drive a measurable action.

buildup.text: She founded Copyhackers and taught thousands of entrepreneurs to write landing pages that actually convert.

discovery.text: Her method: mine customer reviews for exact phrases, then use those words in your copy. Let customers write for you.

twist.text: She increased one client's revenue by 400% by changing a single headline to match customer language. One line.

climax.text: Wiebe proved that modern copywriting is a science of listening. The best copy isn't written—it's extracted.

punchline.text: Listen to customers. They write the best copy for you.

quiz.question: Where does Wiebe's method suggest finding the best copy?

details.whyItMatters: Wiebe bridged traditional copywriting craft and modern growth marketing. Her evidence-based approach gave copywriters a defensible methodology in a metrics-driven digital world.
takeaways: She coined 'conversion copywriting' as a discipline
Her method starts with voice-of-customer research, not brainstorming
Copyhackers became the leading resource for evidence-based copywriting

faq.question: What is conversion copywriting?
faq.answer: It is copy written specifically to move readers toward a measurable action — signing up, purchasing, clicking. Unlike brand copywriting, it combines persuasion principles with testing and optimization. Every word choice is validated against actual conversion data.

faq.question: How does voice-of-customer research improve copywriting?
faq.answer: By mining customer reviews, surveys, and interviews for the exact language customers use to describe their problems and desires. Using customers' own words in copy creates instant recognition and trust — far more effective than guessing what resonates.
